section.heading: Threatening force or violence against groups

content.p: Offences
A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person threatens to use force or violence against a group (the targeted group); and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, intersex status, disability, nationality, national or ethnic origin or political opinion; and
a reasonable member of the targeted group would fear that the threat will be carried out; and
the threat, if carried out, would threaten the peace, order and good government of the Commonwealth.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years.
A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person threatens to use force or violence against a group (the targeted group); and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, intersex status, disability, nationality, national or ethnic origin or political opinion; and
a reasonable member of the targeted group would fear that the threat will be carried out.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years.
The fault element for paragraphs (1)(b) and (2)(b) is recklessness.
Note: For recklessness, see section 5.4.
Strict liability applies to paragraphs (1)(c) and (2)(c).
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(b) and (2)(b), the person may have in mind a combination of attributes mentioned in those paragraphs.
Alternative verdict
(6) Subsection (7) applies if, in a prosecution for an offence (the prosecuted offence) against subsection (1), the trier of fact:
is not satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence; but
(b) is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the defendant is guilty of an offence (the alternative offence) against subsection (2).

The trier of fact may find the defendant not guilty of the prosecuted offence but guilty of the alternative offence, so long as the defendant has been accorded procedural fairness in relation to that finding of guilt.
Definitions
In this section:
fear includes apprehension.

the threat, if carried out, would threaten the peace, order and good government of the Commonwealth.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2.

section.heading: Advocating damage to or destruction of real property or motor vehicle

content.p: Offences
(1) A person (the first person) commits an offence if:
the first person advocates the causing of damage to, or the destruction of, real property or a motor vehicle; and
the first person does so because of the first person’s belief that:
(i) the real property is a place of worship of a group (the targeted group); or
(ii) the real property is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(iii) the motor vehicle is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(iv) the real property is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(v) the motor vehicle is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of a group (the targeted group); and
the first person is reckless as to whether the damage or destruction will occur; and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, intersex status, disability, nationality, national or ethnic origin or political opinion; and
the damage or destruction, if it were to occur, would threaten the peace, order and good government of the Commonwealth.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2. For recklessness, see section 5.4.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years.
(2) A person (the first person) commits an offence if:
the first person advocates the causing of damage to, or the destruction of, real property or a motor vehicle; and
the first person does so because of the first person’s belief that:
(i) the real property is a place of worship of a group (the targeted group); or
(ii) the real property is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(iii) the motor vehicle is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(iv) the real property is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of a group (the targeted group); or
(v) the motor vehicle is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of a group (the targeted group); and
the first person is reckless as to whether the damage or destruction will occur; and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, intersex status, disability, nationality, national or ethnic origin or political opinion.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2. For recklessness, see section 5.4.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years.
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(b) and (2)(b), it is immaterial whether:
the real property actually is a place of worship of the targeted group; or
the real property actually is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of the targeted group; or
the motor vehicle actually is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by one or more members of the targeted group; or
the real property actually is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of the targeted group; or
the motor vehicle actually is owned, or occupied, in whole or in part, by a close associate of one or more members of the targeted group.
The fault element for paragraphs (1)(d) and (2)(d) is recklessness.
Note: For recklessness, see section 5.4.
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(d) and (2)(d), the person may have in mind a combination of attributes mentioned in those paragraphs.
Alternative verdict
(6) Subsection (7) applies if, in a prosecution for an offence (the prosecuted offence) against subsection (1), the trier of fact:
is not satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence; but
(b) is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the defendant is guilty of an offence (the alternative offence) against subsection (2).

The trier of fact may find the defendant not guilty of the prosecuted offence but guilty of the alternative offence, so long as the defendant has been accorded procedural fairness in relation to that finding of guilt.
Definitions
In this section:
advocate means counsel, promote, encourage or urge.

section.heading: Advocating force or violence through causing damage to property

content.p: Offences
(1) A person (the first person) commits an offence if:
(a) the first person intentionally advocates for another person, or a group, to use force or violence against a group (the targeted group); and
the first person does so by causing damage to property; and
the first person does so reckless as to whether the force or violence will occur; and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion or ethnic origin; and
the use of force or violence would threaten the peace, order and good government of the Commonwealth.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2. For recklessness, see section 5.4.
(2) A person (the first person) commits an offence if:
(a) the first person intentionally advocates for another person, or a group, to use force or violence against a group (the targeted group); and
the first person does so by causing damage to property; and
the first person does so reckless as to whether the force or violence will occur; and
the targeted group is distinguished by race, religion or ethnic origin.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years.
Note: For intention, see section 5.2. For recklessness, see section 5.4.
The fault element for paragraphs (1)(d) and (2)(d) is recklessness.
Note: For recklessness, see section 5.4.
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(d) and (2)(d), the person may have in mind a combination of attributes mentioned in those paragraphs.
Alternative verdict
(5) Subsection (6) applies if, in a prosecution for an offence (the prosecuted offence) against subsection (1), the trier of fact:
is not satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence; but
(b) is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the defendant is guilty of an offence (the alternative offence) against subsection (2).

The trier of fact may find the defendant not guilty of the prosecuted offence but guilty of the alternative offence, so long as the defendant has been accorded procedural fairness in relation to that finding of guilt.
Meaning of damage
In this section:
damage includes minor damage.
Example: An offensive slogan painted on a building (advocating the use of force or violence against Jews) is damage for the purposes of this section.

7 Application provision

The amendments made by this Schedule apply in relation to a conviction that occurs on or after the commencement of this item if the conduct constituting the offence occurs wholly on or after that commencement.
8 Review of amendments
The Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security must review the operation and effectiveness of the amendments made by this Schedule.
The Committee must:
begin the review before the end of the period of 2 years beginning on the day on which this Schedule commences; and
report the Committee’s comments and recommendations to each House of the Parliament as soon as practicable after completing the review.
